Executive Summary
01
Why this partnership exists and what success looks like.
Who Standard Meds is
Standard Meds is a US telehealth platform offering compounded prescription medications via licensed physicians and FDA-
registered pharmacies. Each product is a complete clinical program: online health assessment → licensed physician review →
compounded medication shipped → ongoing care via patient portal. The brand covered in this playbook is NeuroCalmRx
(peripheral neuropathy).
What Logicall is taking on
Page 1 of 16

The outbound recovery calls today are placed by an AI voice agent. Pickup and conversion rates aren't where we need them, and
that's the gap Logicall is here to close — human callers, real conversations, recovered revenue. For this funnel, Logicall handles
calls across 2 recoverable stages.
STAGE PRIORITY — CHECKOUT ABANDON IS THE BIGGEST LEVER
The 2 stages don't carry the same weight.
CHECKOUT ABANDON HAS THE LOWEST VOLUME BUT THE HIGHEST CONVERSION CEILING
: the lead already chose a plan, validated their card, and stopped one click before paying. They are the closest to "yes" of any segment
in this playbook. Treat every Checkout Abandon call as priority — it's where the recovered-dollar-per-call is the highest by a wide
margin.
IMPORTANT — QUIZ ABANDONMENT IS NOT RECOVERABLE
The NeuroCalmRx funnel captures name, email and phone
ONLY ON THE LAST QUIZ QUESTION
. If a lead drops out before that, we have zero contact data. There is no "Quiz Abandon" recovery for this product. Recoverable stages
start at Dosage (lead finished the quiz, didn't pick a plan).
The 2 recoverable stages
1. Dosage Abandon — Finished quiz, saw the plans, didn't pick one. (Pricing-active call.)
2. Checkout Abandon — Picked a plan, reached checkout, didn't pay. (Pricing-active call.)
Volume context
Today the funnels produce roughly 20–30 leads per day distributed across the recoverable stages and the live brands. The
split shifts daily and is expected to scale with paid traffic ramps.
Success metrics we'll track together
Pickup rate (live human answers vs. voicemail)
Recovery rate per stage (% of called leads that complete the next funnel step within 72h)
Average call duration vs. target
Compliance rate (TCPA window adherence, opt-out honoring)
The Product at a Glance
02
Read this card before your first call. It contains everything you'll anchor on during a recovery conversation.
NeuroCalmRx
PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY · LDN + B12
A physician-prescribed compound combining Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN) and Methylcobalamin B12. One capsule, 30 seconds
before bed. Compounded at an FDA-registered pharmacy and third-party tested.
Mechanism TLR4 reset via endorphin rebound — microglia stand down, inflammation cools, myelin starts to rebuild.
Authority Dr. Kirten S. Parekh, ABPM board-certified foot & ankle reconstructive surgeon, RDN clinical nutritionist. Stanford
Pain Lab + Journal of Neuroimmune Pharmacology references.
Timeline Sleep (1–2 wk) → tingling softens (m1) → pain measurably lower (m3) → full effect (m5–6).
Guarantee 90-day money-back guarantee.
Tone Empathetic, neurobiological-but-accessible. Validates "I've tried everything."

OFFERS MAY VARY OVER TIME

ONE SHORT RULE THAT CHANGES EVERY CALL
Until a physician has reviewed the lead's assessment,
NOTHING HAS BEEN APPROVED OR PRESCRIBED
. Never say "your physician is ready," "your prescription is approved," or "your medication is ready to ship." Safe phrasing: "After
checkout, a physician reviews your assessment and, if approved, your medication ships."

Per-Stage Playbook
04
Two stages, two cards. Read the card before the call. The opener and discovery questions are calibrated
against real call transcripts — use them as a guide, adjust to your own voice.
Page 9 of 16

Dosage Abandon
CARD 1 / 2
Lead finished the assessment, landed on the dosage page, saw the 1-month / 3-month plans, and didn't pick one. This is the
hottest segment in the funnel — they know the product, saw the price, and stopped one decision short. The objection is almost
never "tell me about the product." It's "which plan is right for me" or "is it worth it."
This is the screen your lead is staring at when you call.
GOAL
Send dosage-page link via SMS
AVG CALL
≤ 5 min
PRICING POSTURE
Active — anchor the bundle
OPENER (≤ 15 SEC)
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} calling from Standard Meds. You completed your neuropathy health assessment
recently and I saw you got all the way to the plan page but didn't pick a dosage yet. I wanted to check in — is this a
good time for a quick call?"
DISCOVERY QUESTION (≤ 45 SEC)
"I noticed you got all the way through the assessment and saw the plans, but didn't pick one — was there a specific
question about which plan is right for you, or anything else that came up?"
ADDRESS — MOST COMMON PATTERNS
"Wasn't sure which plan to pick" → Anchor the recommended bundle proactively: "the 3-month is what most
patients go with — $297, about $99 a month, and it lines up with the clinical window when results really build."
"Price / is it worth it" → Use the per-month math + the 90-day money-back guarantee. The guarantee aligns with
the clinical-results window, so they see results inside the risk-free period.
"Wanted to think about it" → Acknowledge. Offer to send the link so they can revisit with all the info ready.
TANGIBLE ANCHORS (USE WHEN PRICE COMES UP)
Page 10 of 16

NEUROCALMRX — ANCHOR ANGLES
vs Gabapentin / Lyrica: those mute the pain signal but don't address the TLR4 receptor stuck in overdrive — symptoms come
back when the dose wears off
vs supplements (ALA, B12 megadoses): try to nourish nerves under active immune attack — they don't reduce the microglial
inflammation
vs opioids: not only mask symptoms, they also interfere with how LDN works (only category Dr. Parekh's team flags)
NeuroCalm 3-month at $297 ≈ $99/mo — a real prescription compound from an FDA-registered pharmacy, with a 90-day
money-back guarantee
CLOSE
"Can I send you the dosage page link right now so you can pick the plan that fits best? Takes a minute."
ACTION ON YES
Trigger SMS send (the dosage page URL — not checkout, so the patient picks the plan themselves). Verbally confirm:
"Sent — you should see the text any moment. Let me know when it comes through."
VOICEMAIL SCRIPT
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} from Standard Meds. You completed your neuropathy assessment recently and I
just wanted to make sure you had everything you needed to pick a plan. I'll send you a text with your link so you can
take a look when it's convenient. Take care!"
STOP / OPT-OUT
If the lead says "not interested," "stop calling," or expresses any clear refusal: acknowledge it, thank them, end the call,
do not send the link. Flag for suppression.
Checkout Abandon
CARD 2 / 2
Lower volume than Dosage but the single highest-conversion call in the playbook. The lead picked a plan, reached
checkout, validated their card details, and stopped one click before paying. They are the closest segment to "yes" we have.
Something specific stopped them at the final step — typically price hesitation, payment friction, or last-minute "let me think."
They are already informed and already convinced enough to type their card. Don't re-sell from scratch — just remove the
friction.

Objection Library
05
The full bench of rebuttals. These have been calibrated against real call transcripts — use them as guidance,
not scripts to read verbatim.
NeuroCalmRx — Top Objections
Q "I've already tried everything — nothing works."
A "I completely understand — and that frustration is one of the most common things we hear. The reason LDN is different is that it doesn't try
to compete with treatments that mute the signal. It targets the reason the signal won't stop — the TLR4 receptor stuck in overdrive. Most
treatments have never addressed that part. That's why patients who've tried everything else often see results with this one."
Q "Is LDN safe? I've never heard of it."
A "That makes sense — LDN has almost no pharmaceutical marketing behind it because the patent expired decades ago, so there's no
incentive for drug companies to promote it. But the research is real: Stanford Pain Lab, the Journal of Neuroimmune Pharmacology. It's been
used in clinical settings since the 1980s. At the micro-dose used in NeuroCalm, the safety profile is very well established."
Q "Will it interact with my other medications?"
A "That's an important question and Dr. Parekh's team reviews every patient's medication list before approving the prescription. LDN is
compatible with the vast majority of medications. The one category to watch is opioid pain medications — LDN can interfere with how they
work. If you're on opioids, the care team would discuss that specifically with you."
Q "How long before I feel something?"
A "Most patients notice something in sleep first — fewer wake-ups, easier to fall back asleep. That usually happens in the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Pain reduction tends to follow, and it builds over months rather than happening all at once. The full effect takes time because your nervous
system is literally rebuilding — that's a good thing, it means real change."
Q "It's expensive / I need a cheaper option."
A "Totally hear you — and the way the pricing is set up actually matters for the result. The one-month is $169. The three-month is $297, which
works out to about ninety-nine dollars a month — roughly a forty-percent saving per month. The reason most patients go with the three-
month isn't just the saving — it's that the clinical window where pain really drops is month two and three. One month only gets you through the
sleep-improvement phase. Three months lines up with the 90-day guarantee, so you see a full results window inside the risk-free period."
Page 13 of 16

Q "How do I know this isn't a scam?"
A "Completely fair question. NeuroCalm Rx is a real prescription compound — it goes through an FDA-registered pharmacy, it's tested by
third-party labs, and Dr. Parekh attaches his medical license to a 90-day money-back guarantee. If that guarantee wasn't backed by real
clinical confidence, no physician would put their license on the line for it."
Q "I need to think about it / talk to my doctor."
A "Of course — that's a reasonable thing to do. If it helps, you can share the information with your doctor — the mechanism is peer-reviewed
and the research is published. Is there anything specific I can help clarify before you have that conversation?"
Compliance & Operational Rules
06
The non-negotiables. Standard Meds operates under federal telehealth regulation, FDA-registered
pharmacy oversight, and TCPA. A bad call can cost a license, a patient's trust, or both. Read this twice.
Always
Self-identify
"I'm {your name} from Standard Meds. I'm not a doctor." Required on every call, every time. If asked "are you a robot," answer honestly.
Honor TCPA
9:00am – 9:00pm in the lead's local timezone. Period. If a lead is in PT and it's 9:05pm there, do not call.
Recording disclosure
Where required by state, disclose recording at the start. Logicall's dialer should handle the consent prompt automatically.
Stop on opt-out
"Stop calling," "not interested," "don't contact me again" — acknowledge, end the call, flag for permanent suppression. Do not reattempt.
One product, one call
The lead came in through one funnel. Don't cross-sell another brand. Stay on the product they qualified for.
Send the link, end the call
Two re-offers maximum after objection. After that, end gracefully. Never push.
Never
Never invent discounts
If asked, say: "I'll pass that to the care team — they handle pricing flexibility." Never promise a code, a coupon, or a discount that isn't
already on the live checkout.
Never claim approval before review
Until physician review, the prescription has not been approved. Don't say "your prescription is ready," "approved," "shipping soon."
Never make medical claims
Page 14 of 16

No "this will cure your neuropathy." Never diagnose. If pressed on a medical question, defer: "your physician can answer that during the
assessment review."
Never create false urgency
No "limited spots," "offer expires today," "last chance." If you need urgency, use the medical reality: "the cellular renewal cycle interrupts
between bottles."
Never trigger a link send to voicemail
Voicemail = leave the script, do not invoke the "send link" action. The lead has not consented to receive an SMS in that interaction.

Three rules to memorize
RULE 1 — THE LINK IS THE TRANSACTION
Your single goal on every call is a verbal "yes, send me the link." Once you have it, send and end. Don't keep selling.
RULE 2 — TWO OBJECTIONS, THEN RE-OFFER
Address the first objection with empathy, address the second with the anchor, re-offer the link. After the second re-offer, if they still
decline, end gracefully. Never push to a third.
RULE 3 — NOTHING IS APPROVED UNTIL PHYSICIAN REVIEW
Until a physician has reviewed the assessment, do not say "approved," "ready," "shipping." Safe phrasing: "After checkout, a physician
reviews your assessment and if approved your medication ships."

If a lead asks about returns, terms, or privacy on a call, the safe move is "let me text you the policy" — never paraphrase. These
pages are the legally binding versions and Standard Meds keeps them up to date:
